claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is SUPERSEDED.
In CodePipeline's SUPERSEDED execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In SUPERSEDED mode, a newer execution can overtake an older execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it starts.
In a CodePipeline pipeline with a CodeBuild stage running pulumi up, a queued execution waiting behind a busy stage can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting CodePipeline execution mode to QUEUED makes waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn.
CodePipeline QUEUED execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
The AWS CLI create-pipeline/update-pipeline commands accept executionMode and pipelineType settings for a pipeline.
The Pulumi aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource has executionMode and pipelineType inputs.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from deploying at once.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is set on the stage that references the environment with the exclusive lock check.
The default value of Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, one at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider offers an `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
The link targets /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ and /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exist.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
In TeamCity, the build configuration's advanced option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0 (unlimited) and is found under the configuration's General Settings.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 queues a second build behind the first, and it runs only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists as the update conflict page.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by the deployment job, together with `lockBehavior: sequential` on the stage, serializes deployments.
Azure Pipelines YAML stages accept a `lockBehavior` property with the value `sequential`.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an execution mode setting that can be set to `QUEUED`, so waiting executions run in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'; setting it to 1 serializes builds.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
